disclaimer: Decision-support prototype, not a medical device.

routine.when: Every Sol, right after waking: before breakfast, coffee or exercise.
routine.why: Same time and conditions every Sol make today's numbers comparable with your own normal.

status_rules.ACT: any indicator red -> contact the flight surgeon
status_rules.WATCH: any indicator amber, or any value different from your personal baseline (|z| >= 2) -> self-care action

indicators.label: Resting heart rate
indicators.range_text: Green 50-100 bpm · Amber 40-49 or 101-120 · Red <40 or >120
indicators.how_to_measure: Sit still for 5 minutes after waking. Use the pulse sensor, or count beats at your wrist for 30 seconds and multiply by 2.
indicators.why_it_matters_in_space: Weightlessness (gravity hazard) de-conditions the heart and blood vessels; a resting pulse that drifts tells you early.

thresholds.where_in_source: Sinus bradycardia defined as sinus rate <50 bpm

sources.citation: Assumption of this project (no source found for this exact cut-off).

Kusumoto FM et al. 2018 ACC/AHA/HRS Guideline on the Evaluation and Management of Patients With Bradycardia and Cardiac Conduction Delay. Heart Rhythm 2019;16(9):e128-e226 (also Circulation 2019;140:e382-e482). Sinus bradycardia: sinus rate <50 bpm; normal 50-100 bpm (ACC press release).
sources.access: ACC 'Guidelines Made Simple' table and ACC press release; full guideline text not read

sources.citation: American Heart Association. All About Heart Rate (Pulse): a resting heart rate of 60 to 100 beats per minute is normal for most adults; well-trained athletes can be lower.
sources.access: via secondary sources quoting the AHA page (AARP, Fortune); heart.org not reachable from our build environment

indicators.label: Blood pressure
indicators.how_to_measure: Sit 5 minutes, feet flat, cuff on bare upper arm at heart level. Don't talk. Take 2 readings 1 minute apart and enter the second.
indicators.why_it_matters_in_space: Without gravity (gravity hazard) body fluids shift to the head; blood pressure control changes and can fail when standing up again on Mars.

sources.citation: Assumption of this project (no source found for this exact cut-off).

MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine). Low Blood Pressure: 'If your blood pressure reading is 90/60 or lower, you have low blood pressure.' Low readings matter mainly when they cause symptoms.

American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology. 2025 AHA/ACC/multisociety Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults. Blood pressure categories unchanged from the 2017 guideline (Whelton PK et al., Hypertension 2018;71:e13-e115, doi:10.1161/HYP.0000000000000065): Normal <120 and <80; Elevated 120-129 and <80; Stage 1 130-139 or 80-89; Stage 2 >=140 or >=90 mmHg.
sources.access: category cut-offs confirmed via guideline summaries (AHA professional 'Top things to know', Harvard Health); heart.org page not reachable from our build environment

indicators.label: Blood sugar (fasting)
indicators.how_to_measure: Before eating or drinking anything but water (8 h fast). Wash and dry your fingertip, prick the side, use the second drop on the meter strip.
indicators.why_it_matters_in_space: Inactivity, stress hormones and an altered diet in a closed habitat (closed-environment hazard) can disturb how your body handles sugar.

thresholds.where_in_source: Diabetes range: fasting plasma glucose >=126 mg/dL (needs confirmation)

sources.citation: International Hypoglycaemia Study Group. Glucose concentrations of less than 3.0 mmol/L (54 mg/dL) should be reported in clinical trials: a joint position statement of the ADA and EASD. Diabetes Care 2017;40(1):155-157. Adopted in ADA Standards of Care Section 6 (Glycemic Goals and Hypoglycemia): Level 1 <70 mg/dL, Level 2 <54 mg/dL.
sources.access: long-standing ADA classification; 2026 Section 6 text not re-read for this release

sources.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026. Diabetes Care 49(Suppl 1). Fasting plasma glucose 100-125 mg/dL = prediabetes; >=126 mg/dL = diabetes range (fasting = no caloric intake for >=8 h; diagnosis needs confirmation).
sources.access: thresholds confirmed via 2026 Standards summaries (PMC, Guideline Central); full section not read

indicators.label: Body temperature
indicators.how_to_measure: Thermometer under the tongue, mouth closed, for the full beep. No hot or cold drinks for 15 minutes before.
indicators.why_it_matters_in_space: In a closed habitat (closed-environment hazard) infections spread easily and spaceflight weakens immunity; resting body temperature also runs ~1 °C higher on long missions.

thresholds.where_in_source: Upper green edge set with STAHN_2017 in mind: resting core temperature runs ~1 C higher on long missions, so a slightly raised reading alone is not red.

sources.citation: Hypothermia. StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf NBK545239): hypothermia = core body temperature below 35 C (95 F); mild 32-35 C.
Assumption of this project (no source found for this exact cut-off).
US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Definitions of Signs, Symptoms, and Conditions of Ill Travelers: fever = measured temperature of 100.4 F (38 C) or greater.

indicators.label: Sleep last night
indicators.range_text: Green 7-9 h · Amber 6-6.9 or 9.1-10 h · Red <6 or >10 h
indicators.how_to_measure: Count hours actually asleep (not time in the sleep bag). Use your sleep tracker if you wear one.
indicators.why_it_matters_in_space: No natural day/night, noise and confinement (isolation hazard) disrupt sleep; tired crew make more mistakes during critical tasks.

thresholds.where_in_source: Adults 26-64: recommended 7-9 h; 6 h may be appropriate
Adults 26-64: recommended 7-9 h; 10 h may be appropriate

sources.citation: Hirshkowitz M et al. National Sleep Foundation's sleep time duration recommendations: methodology and results summary. Sleep Health 1(1):40-43 (2015). Adults 26-64: recommended 7-9 h; may be appropriate 6 h and 10 h; not recommended <6 h or >10 h.

indicators.label: Mood
indicators.how_to_measure: Pick the face that best matches how you have felt since waking: 1 = very low, 3 = okay, 5 = great.
indicators.why_it_matters_in_space: Months of isolation and confinement far from Earth (isolation and distance hazards) wear down mood and team cohesion.
